related_questions.question: What is the best medicine to take if you have COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: For most people with mild COVID-19, over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil) can help manage symptoms. Prescription antiviral medications, such as Paxlovid, are available for those at higher risk of severe illness, but these should be taken as directed by a doctor. It's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional to determine the most appropriate treatment plan based on individual health conditions and risk factors.

list.snippet: Acetaminophen (Tylenol): Helps reduce fever and pain.
Ibuprofen (Advil): Also helps reduce fever and pain.

text_blocks.snippet: Prescription medications (for those at higher risk):

list.snippet: Paxlovid: An antiviral medication that can reduce the severity and duration of COVID-19.
Other antiviral medications: A doctor may prescribe other antivirals based on individual needs.

list.title: Consult a doctor:
list.snippet: If you have symptoms of COVID-19, especially if you are at higher risk for severe illness, it's essential to talk to a doctor to determine the best course of treatment.

list.title: Early treatment:
list.snippet: Prescription medications like Paxlovid are most effective when started soon after symptom onset.

list.title: Drug interactions:
list.snippet: Paxlovid can interact with other medications, so it's important to inform your doctor about all medications you are taking, according to the CDC.
